candidate.title: RASL-seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina poster’s RASL-seq row: poly(A)+ RNA → targeted DNA-probe annealing → ligation → bead selection → elution → sample-indexed library. This is a schematic architecture with primary-paper interpretation of the material carrier, capture and indexing interfaces. The drawing’s ligation-before-selection order is preserved and explicitly distinguished from the selection-before-ligation implementation in Li, Qiu and Fu (2012). The final Indexed cDNA label is retained as source wording and resolved as a DNA probe-amplicon library. Adjacent CaptureSeq and ClickSeq rows, the lower cropped row and the far-right chemical structure belong to the surrounding poster rather than alternative targets of the RASL-seq card. The endpoint is the indexed library; readout meaning is explained without adding unshown sequencing, pooling or specimen-preparation operations.

states.label: Poly A+ RNA
features: Biological target: polyadenylated RNA; drawn with a 5′OH and a 3′ poly(A) tail. The RNA 5′OH is distinct from the phosphate on a DNA targeting probe.
The depicted route starts at poly(A)+ RNA; the paper also permits total RNA or lysate inputs, but those preparation alternatives are outside this assigned row.

states.label: Adjacent targeted DNA probe pair with common index and P5 primer arms
features: Two DNA oligonucleotides hybridize to adjacent target sequences on an RNA, typically across a selected exon–exon junction. The paper specifies a 20 nt target-complementary segment on each probe.

The index-primer-bearing probe has a 5′ phosphate at the ligation junction and its common index primer sequence toward its 3′ end. The partner has its common P5 sequence toward its 5′ end and the facing 3′OH at the junction.
The labelled primer arms are part of the targeting probes; the RNA itself is not an amplification primer or a cDNA intermediate.

states.label: Indexed DNA probe-amplicon library (diagram label: Indexed cDNA)
features: PCR products derived from synthetic ligated DNA probes, carrying P5/P7 sequencing interfaces and a sample barcode; no RNA-to-cDNA conversion is shown or required by this implementation.
The target read covers the joined probe-recognition region (40 nt in the primary implementation). The index read assigns that probe tag to a sample.

Expected probe-tag counts report abundance of preselected transcripts or designed splice-junction targets within each sample. Probe-dependent ligation efficiencies and unintended ligation products limit interpretation; surviving capture does not prove perfect biological specificity.
Because the sequenced target region is supplied by designed probes, this readout is restricted to the selected panel and does not provide unrestricted transcript sequence or novel isoform discovery.

operations.label: Add targeted primers
operations.description: Anneal the two target-specific DNA probes to adjacent RNA sites and the biotinylated oligo(dT) to the poly(A) tail, producing an RNA-associated probe/capture complex. The visible primer arms and reactive ends position the DNA probes for ligation.
operations.mechanism: Complementary hybridization; no reverse transcription is involved.
operations.information_effect: The chosen probe pair supplies target recognition. Where designed across an exon–exon junction, adjacent binding encodes the selected junction rather than an entire transcript.

operations.label: Ligate
operations.description: Join the aligned DNA probes into a single continuous probe on the RNA template, retaining the common index and P5 arms. The graph retains the poster’s local order before Selection. The primary implementation instead selects the RNA-bound probes before ligation (c_order).
operations.mechanism: The paper identifies T4 DNA ligase. Ligation joins the facing DNA 5′ phosphate and 3′OH; RNA acts as the hybridization template, not as the ligated or copied product.
operations.information_effect: Converts adjacent probe recognition into an amplifiable DNA tag. A joined pair is evidence for an intended target only to the extent supported by its design and specificity; unrelated-probe ligation can occur.

operations.label: Selection
operations.description: In the drawing, attach the RNA-associated ligated probe complex to streptavidin beads through poly(A)-bound biotinylated oligo(dT), producing a bead-attached selected complex. The capture chemistry is interpreted from the primary source; this post-ligation local instance preserves the drawing and must not be mistaken for the primary protocol’s pre-ligation selection.
operations.mechanism: Oligo(dT)/poly(A) hybridization provides RNA capture specificity and biotin/streptavidin binding provides solid-support attachment. Biotin belongs to the capture oligo, rather than a covalent modification of mRNA.
operations.information_effect: Retains probe material associated with captured polyadenylated RNA. This selects for RNA association and does not guarantee that all retained or subsequently sequenced ligation products are specific.

operations.label: Elute fragment
operations.description: Release the ligated DNA probe from its RNA template into the recovered fraction, changing it from an RNA/bead-associated species to a free DNA fragment available for indexing. The diagram retains only this eluted-product route.
operations.mechanism: The paper explicitly releases ligated probes from their templates and recovers the supernatant; no copying or cleavage of the target RNA is needed to create this product.
operations.information_effect: Target recognition is now carried by the released synthetic ligation product; the biological RNA is not transferred into the sequencing library.

operations.label: Add bar-coded P7 primer
operations.description: Use the barcoded P7/index primer with the common P5 primer in the paper-supported barcoding PCR to amplify the eluted ligated DNA probes and produce a sample-indexed library. This resolves the chemistry inside the schematic’s final broad block; the depicted endpoint is labelled Indexed cDNA.
operations.mechanism: PCR copies the ligated DNA probe template while introducing the P7/sample-barcode interface; P5 and P7 provide Illumina-compatible library ends. This is DNA amplification, not reverse transcription.
operations.information_effect: Physically links each designed target probe tag to its originating sample barcode. Sequencing can associate expected ligation-product identity with sample identity and count those tags for targeted expression or junction measurements. The barcode does not establish original-molecule counts.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and middle-row heading identify RASL-seq as the sole target. All five local operations belong to that depicted route. The matching collection page is headed RASL-Seq and reproduces this same sequence, supporting its catalogue identity; it is secondary evidence. Full-text Li et al. establishes the intended RNA-templated DNA-probe assay and PCR indexing. The graph records the poster’s local material histories; c_order resolves that those local histories should not be read as the primary protocol’s actual selection/ligation sequence. This is a resolved schematic-level assignment, not a claim of equivalence between differently ordered full implementations. Targeted RNA recognition, rather than the broad surrounding RNA Transcription heading, determines the biological readout.
